paper_error_found.claim: Theorem 7.19 completeness: every least common standard multiple has exactly P = max_i max(rd_i, cd_i) columns; get-admissible-shapes returns only such shapes
paper_error_found.reason: P ignores the shape-containment constraint lambda contains shape(f) union shape(g); here that union is (2,1), already two columns
paper_error_found.second_error: the worked example in applications.tex lists 12 bitableaux as LCM(f,g); f lt-divides none of the three shape-(3,3,2) ones checked. It shows the unfiltered line-9 output. Under the algorithm as written the answer is 3, all of shape (3,2,2).
paper_error_found.consequence: leastness has no cheap closed-form certificate; verify() must enumerate the one-column-smaller divisors

hidden_term_order_idea.reason_1: not this paper's mathematics: the bideterminant term order (Definition 7.6) is a single fixed order, and a Robbiano-style weight characterisation of pseudo-ASL term orders is the paper's Open Question 10.4
hidden_term_order_idea.reason_2: the valid answers form a full-dimensional Groebner cone (Mora-Robbiano 1988); recovering it is leading-term choice plus one LP
hidden_term_order_idea.measurement: toric ideals, from-scratch Buchberger over Q, weight order tie-broken by lex, 250 random weight vectors per instance
